## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

 Modern scholarship similarly notes that this tale of the frog hearing the Dharma and gaining miraculous rebirth is framed through commentary and circulated widely across Theravāda literature and its East Asian transmission via texts such as the *Shanjianlü* [Hsu 2018].

**Sources**

- [Hsu 2018] Alexander Ong Hsu, Practices of Scriptural Economy: Compiling and Copying a Seventh-Century Chinese Buddhist Anthology (2018) — Alternative English title and discussion of the frog story's commentary, transmission, and connection to the Visuddhimagga and Shanjianlü.
